history.dynasty: Holkar era (Maratha Indore); commissioned by Shri Dadhich
history.summary: Named 'Bada' (big) for its 25-feet-tall idol of Lord Ganesha on a 14-foot platform, among the largest Ganesh idols in the world, near Rajwada at the western end of MG Road. As per the widely repeated account, Shri Dadhich, a resident of nearby Ujjain (then Avantika), had a dream-vision of Lord Ganesha in 1875 and commissioned the temple; skilled artisans from Rajasthan built the idol from limestone, jaggery, bricks, soil and water gathered from pilgrimage sites including Ujjain, Ayodhya, Mathura, Varanasi and Kashi, powder of five gems (Pancha Ratna: diamond, pearl, emerald, ruby, topaz), with frames said to be of gold, silver, iron and copper. The idol receives a new 'chola' (covering) four times a year in a 15-day ritual using about 15 kg of ghee and 25 kg of sindoor. FLAG: one source (templetravel.info) claims the temple was established in 1735 by Ahilyabai Holkar with an idol found in a well, and trawell.in cites a variant date of 1775 under Ahilyabai Holkar — these conflict with the dominant 1875 Dadhich account and are flagged as unverified.

name: Bada Ganpati Temple
town_description: Indore, the largest city and commercial capital of Madhya Pradesh, lies on the Malwa Plateau at the confluence of the Kanh and Saraswati rivers. A former Holkar princely capital, it is famed for its Maratha-era palaces and temples (notably Rajwada), a celebrated street-food culture, and rapid modern growth including a metro and smart-city infrastructure.

travel.airport: Devi Ahilyabai Holkar Airport, Indore (~8 km; verify)
travel.road: At Bada Ganpati Square near the western end of MG Road, close to Rajwada; easily reached by city bus, auto-rickshaw and taxi

visitor_information.opening_hours: 5:00 AM to 12:00 PM and 4:00 PM to 8:00 PM (trawell.in; verify). Morning aarti 8:00–8:30 AM, evening aarti 7:00–8:00 PM (vedaz.io; verify)
